Jared (Acme): Hey -- our org credits showed 0 this morning even though our billing cycle should've reset at midnight local time. We're blocked. Account org_id: org_8721. Anyone seen this? :grimacing:
Maya (Support): Hi Jared, sorry about that. Just to confirm: are you expecting the refill at midnight in your account timezone or midnight UTC? We normally run resets at 00:00 UTC.
Jared (Acme): We were told 'monthly refill' so we expected local midnight (PDT). Our PMs scheduled a heavy overnight batch and it hit at 00:30 local and drained remaining credits. We thought it would refill at local midnight and it didn't. The portal still shows 0.
Maya (Support): Can you paste the response headers from one of the 429s (if available)? Also did you see any X-Redwood-Quota headers?
Jared (Acme): Here's one from our logs (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 07:31:12 GMT
x-request-id: rwd-9a1b2c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 3600
X-Redwood-Quota-Org: 0/500000
```
Jared (Acme): Portal shows "Org credits remaining: 0 / 500,000" and billing page shows next refill: Mar 1 00:00 (but no timezone indicated).
Maya (Support): Thanks. I'm going to pull your org logs and check the reset job traces. @lena_billing can you confirm whether there were any proration/top-up glitches for org_8721 on the cycle boundary?
Lena (Billing): Looking now. I can see a reset job executed at 00:00:00 UTC for the global tenant. However there's an odd pattern: a background worker from one of your sub-projects sent a burst at 00:00:45 UTC that consumed ~120k tokens in one request (large embedding job). That request was accepted by a host that had not yet synced the quota-reset state. It looks like the reset and the consumption overlapped. We're seeing inconsistent state across our quota shards.
Sam (Eng): This smells like a race between reset cron and shard propagation. We use a multi-shard quota cache with eventual sync. Normally we have a gate that prevents consumption during reset window but I see a gap in metrics where the gate wasn't applied for a few seconds. Repro steps I ran locally:
```
# repro script (simplified)
for i in {1..3}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-xxl","input":"batch..."}'
done
```
When the reset job runs concurrently, one shard may still report old remaining >0 and accept the request, then billing service applies reset which leads to double-consumption semantics.
Maya (Support): So that explains why the portal shows 0 after the overnight batch — credits were drained after we thought reset had applied. Is there any immediate fix? Customer is blocked until tomorrow's refill at 00:00 UTC if we don't intervene.
Lena (Billing): We can do a manual interim top-up for org_8721 to unblock them. I can apply a one-time override of 500k tokens (internal ticket BILL-6421). That will show up in the portal within ~5 minutes. We'll also mark the event for audit. @jared_acme do you want us to proceed with the manual top-up?
Jared (Acme): Yes please. That would be great. Also can you confirm how monthly usage is shown historically? We need to reconcile what consumed tokens so our SREs can fix the batch timing.
Sam (Eng): We'll attach request traces for the window 00:00:00–00:01:30 UTC and highlight the large calls. Also note: the client had two API keys (project-level) so requests went to different routing pools. The shard that accepted the large request hadn't yet pulled the reset marker. We're going to push a patch: make the reset job perform an atomic increment (write-to-durable-first) and add a short read-lock on shards for +/- 2s around the cron.
Maya (Support): I'll action the manual top-up now and confirm when it's done. Jared, once top-up completes, can you retry your blocked job? If you prefer, we can also temporarily increase your burst quota for the next 24h while the fix rolls out.
Quota-bot: Automated action: manual credit override of +500000 tokens queued (BILL-6421). ETA: 4 minutes.
Maya (Support): Top-up completed, portal should show 500,000 available. Jared, can you retry?
Jared (Acme): Confirmed — portal shows 500k. I retried the batch (small test run) and it went through. Thanks!
Lena (Billing): Filed follow-up: BILL-6421 assigned to billing infra. We're adding an end-to-end test for reset + concurrent consumption. Also adding clearer timezone label on the billing UI (will show "Resets at 00:00 UTC" and localised tooltip).
Sam (Eng): Patch queued: ENG-Q678. Deployment target: next minor release (hotfix) in 48 hours. Workaround for now: schedule heavy jobs for 00:05 UTC or check for X-Redwood-Reset header right after midnight.
Jared (Acme): Appreciate the quick help. Could you also add a note to the org settings reminding owners that resets are UTC? Some of our team assumed local midnight.
Maya (Support): Will do — I'll add a support article and pin it in the billing settings, and notify you when the UI tooltip is live. Closing the support escalation now but we'll post follow-ups in this thread. :thumbsup:
Jared (Acme): Thanks all!
Sam (Eng): Leaving the thread with traces attached to BILL-6421. We'll follow up once the patch is deployed.
Lena (Billing): Closing billing action after audit review.
Maya (Support): Thread resolved. If anything else pops up, reopen or DM me. :)
